newsitem.title: UK: WH Smith profits jump, Xmas sales up 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: WH Smith profits jump, Xmas sales up 3 pct.

text.p: British bookseller and newspaper and magazine distribution group W.H. Smith Group Plc said on Wednesday pretax profits more than doubled in the first half, but retail sales over Christmas were just three percent higher.

The retailer's profits rose to 38.6 million pounds ($62.27 million) in the six months to November 30 from 17.3 million. Sales from continuing businesses rose 2 percent to 1.29 billion pounds. December sales from retail operations were up six percent overall and ahead three percent like-for-like.
WH Smith profits jump, Xmas sales up 3 pct

The company, striving to turnaround its performance after a loss last year, said costs were reduced by nine million pounds in the first half. It held its interim dividend unchanged at 5.25 pence per share.

Chief executive Bill Cockburn called the results a step in the right direction, but added in a statement, "there is a great deal more to be done to produce a sustainable trend of improved sales, profits and shareholder value."

In the longer seven-month period to the end of December, the group's cumulative sales grew by a slightly slower 3.0 percent, and by 2.0 percent like-for-like. Smith's net trading profit margins in the first half improved to 3.4 percent from 2.6 percent in the year-ago period. ($1=.6199 Pound)
